A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material support comparison, including matching appendix content across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original editing experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1 and 3, a 25-participant user study in Table 2, and supplementary visual results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and user-study results, and adds E3DGE comparisons, class-agnostic object-editing examples and simultaneous-editing demonstrations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, triplane localization and fusion, encoder fine-tuning, and the loss functions remain unchanged. The new demonstrations do not document an altered algorithm. The proposed attention-based extension is future work, not an implemented component.

E1.justification: v3 adds class-agnostic object editing using LN3Diff and InstantMesh, including vases, chairs and figurines in Figure 1. This substantially broadens coverage beyond the earlier face, head and clothing domains. Figure 13 also introduces a multiple-reference attribute-composition scenario; previous coverage is retained.

E2.justification: E3DGE is added to the actual comparisons in Table 1 and Figure 6, with hair-editing results and eyeglasses marked unsupported. The original twelve comparators remain.

E3.justification: The added qualitative experiments introduce LN3Diff and InstantMesh backbones and a three-reference configuration supplying hair, eyes and lips in Figure 13. The existing CelebA metrics, encoder-training schedule and 25-participant user-study procedure are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 13 adds a qualitative case study of composing several attributes from separate references. The component ablations in Table 3 and Figure 8, stylization examples, and supplementary examples illustrating user-study responses are retained.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests, and the user-study sample size and percentage reporting remain the same.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds E3DGE hair results: FID 77.86, masked SSIM 0.8083, masked L2 0.0257 and time 1.2 seconds. Existing numerical results, including Tables 2 and 3, are unchanged. Qualitative additions include object edits and simultaneous edits, while Figure 11 replaces full-head examples. These additions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, including Equations 1-5 and supplementary Equation 6, is unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v3 introduces no new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and third contribution explicitly add applicability to class-agnostic objects. The central claims about reference-based 3D-aware triplane editing, source preservation and state-of-the-art comparisons retain their earlier meaning.

C2.justification: v3 removes the limitation concerning fusion between generators with incompatible decoder weights, without documenting its resolution. It adds dependence on reconstruction quality and a future-work conjecture about joint DiT token processing and attention-based fusion eliminating canonical alignment.

D1.justification: The optimizer, learning rate, training budget, hardware, supplementary processing code and parameter defaults are retained. The project link is relocated, and the code gains listing captions. The new object demonstrations provide no detailed implementation recipe.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations concerning E3DGE, diffusion editing and large 3D reconstruction/generation models, connecting the object extension and future work to this literature. Existing cited works and the main novelty positioning are retained; publication-metadata updates are not new references.

P1.justification: Prose is selectively tightened, the conclusion is shortened, and object-generalization and future-work paragraphs are added. Supplementary subsections A.1-A.3 become Sections 6-8 under a separate supplementary heading. Most narrative structure and explanations remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned, Table 1 and Figure 6 accommodate E3DGE, Figure 11 replaces examples, and Figure 13 is added. Some figures move within the layout. Existing supplementary images are retained and renumbered, while the code moves into captioned listings.

improvement.justification: The added 3D comparator and object/composition demonstrations modestly strengthen empirical support while preserving the existing experiments and appendix evidence. The benefit is limited by sparse implementation details for the object extension and removal of the explicit decoder-compatibility limitation.
